stories.title: The United States Capitol
stories.summary: The Capitol stands at the eastern end of the National Mall and houses the Senate and the House of Representatives.

location.note: Rounded pin at the east end of the National Mall. A surveyed building coordinate is [UNKNOWN] in this episode. Not a street address.

stories.script: Story one. The United States Capitol stands at the eastern end of the National Mall in Washington, D.C. The Senate and the House of Representatives meet here to craft the country's laws. The pin is approximate.

cards.title: U.S. Capitol
cards.body: The United States Capitol Building is in Washington, D.C., at the eastern end of the National Mall. At the Capitol the Senate and the House of Representatives come together to discuss, debate and deliberate national policy and craft the country's laws.
cards.why: A clear, official landmark on the offline DC region pack, used here as the first beat of a short story demo.

stories.title: The Lincoln Memorial
stories.summary: The Lincoln Memorial is in National Mall and Memorial Parks. From there the Mall stretches toward the Washington Monument and the U.S. Capitol.

location.name: Lincoln Memorial (approx.)
location.note: Rounded pin west of the Capitol pin, inside the DC region pack bbox. A surveyed memorial coordinate is [UNKNOWN] in this episode. Not a street address.

stories.script: Story two. The Lincoln Memorial is in National Mall and Memorial Parks in Washington, D.C. From the memorial the Mall looks east toward the Washington Monument and the U.S. Capitol. The pin is approximate.

captions.text: National Mall and Memorial Parks, Washington, D.C.
The Mall looks east toward the Capitol. Pin is approximate.

cards.title: Lincoln Memorial
cards.body: The Lincoln Memorial is a National Park Service memorial in the District of Columbia, in National Mall and Memorial Parks. A National Park Service view looks east from the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool toward the Washington Monument and the U.S. Capitol. The National Mall is shown as a stretch from the Lincoln Memorial to the U.S. Capitol.
cards.why: A second official landmark inside the same offline region pack, used to test two-story playback and resume.
